(1) the stochastic activity network (SAN) is an excellent model for representing a wide variety of complex systems; (2) the SAN model can be constructed by standard techniques, but the size of the resulting state space may be prohibitive for practical solution; (3) the size of the state space of the SAN can be greatly reduced through the application of symmetry-based techniques; and (4) the resulting model is suitable for practical solution of the measures of interest.
the use of reduced base models for SANs can yield dramatic reductions of state-space size while still permitting solution of the desired measures by traditional techniques.

the development of efficient and effective techniques for stochastic analysis of large, complex computer systems and networks.
